newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa says her prayers as she recovers.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa says her prayers as she recovers.

text.p: Mother Teresa was gradually recovering from heart trouble on Saturday and said her morning prayers in an intensive care unit, her doctor said.
"As of now she is doing well," Dr S.K. Sen, medical director of Woodlands Nursing Home in the eastern Indian city of Calcutta, told reporters.
The 86-year-old Roman Catholic missionary was rushed to hospital with an irregular heart beat early on Friday, the third time since August that she had been taken to Woodlands for emergency care.
"She is responding very well to the treatment. She is breathing normally," Sen said. Her heart rate was being controlled but would take some time before becoming fully normal, he said.
"We want to watch for another 24 hours. Only after then will we take a decision when she will be released. Probably on Monday we will be able to tell you."

The hospital issued a medical bulletin saying the 1979 Nobel Peace Prize winner, who is fitted with a heart pacemaker, was gradually improving. "She is alert and cheeful. She is on a normal diet," it said.
"She had her usual morning prayers," the physician said, adding that Mother Teresa had spoken to some nuns from her Missionaries of Charity religious order in her hospital room.
Since she was fitted with the heart pacemaker in 1989, Mother Teresa has spent time in hospital for heart disease, bacterial pneumonia, broken ribs, malaria, and lung problems.
She spent nearly three weeks at Woodlands in late August and early September for heart trouble, malaria and pneumonia.
Two weeks after returning to her Calcutta-based order, she fell off a chair and hit her head. A brain scan revealed and she was later relleased.
Last Saturday, Mother Teresa received honorary American citizenship, one of only five people in U.S. history, in a ceremony led by U.S. Ambassador to India Frank Wisner.
She began her life's work in the slums of Calcutta, India's most densely populated city, in 1949 and has won worldwide admiration for her devotion to the poor.
